label: PBI report build
info: Builds the pbi_* tables of eu_report/pbi_report/report from the CSV files in the data lake (step 1: machine names, shift names, calendar). No API calls. Needs the Config tab.

name: [1] TRIGGER & TASK SETTINGS
info: STAGE 1 - TRIGGER AND TASK SETTINGS. Builds the Power BI tables of eu_report/pbi_report/report from the CSV files in the data lake. This step: pbi_machine_names (Machine Names files of the sites, with the filters of the report queries), pbi_shift_naming (the distinct shifts of the Shift Patterns file), pbi_calendar (generated). The inject payload is the job: {"tables": [...], "sites": [...]}; a missing list means all tables, all sites. Nothing is written while the table is true in DRY_RUN of 1.1.

name: 1.1 TASK SETTINGS (edit here)
1.2 Start jobs
[2] MACHINE NAMES: FILES
info: STAGE 2 - one message per site: the folder eu_report/reference/machine_names/site=<Site>/ is listed, the newest .csv file is read and parsed (header row, one message with all rows), and the rows of the site are built with the filters of the report queries (Hull: no "GT4 - Auto", Dept Dries Pack or Liquids Pack; Nottingham: Area SD Packing or Strepsils Packing; Weinheim: all). A site without a file gives a failed item: then nothing is written for the table.

2.2 Pick the file
2.3 Build machine rows
[3] pbi_machine_names
info: STAGE 3 - the join waits for the items of all sites, collect puts the rows in one list, decide writes nothing when a site failed or in dry-run mode, then parquet, path and write object. Unique Machine Name = machine name + "-" + site, as in the report. One file for all sites.

3.2 Decide pbi_machine_names

[4] SHIFT NAMES: FILE
info: STAGE 4 - the folder eu_report/reference/shift_naming/site=All/ is listed, the newest .csv file (Shift Patterns Provideam EU, columns ShiftName and Shift) is read and parsed, one row per line.

4.2 Pick the file
4.3 Build shift rows
[5] pbi_shift_naming
info: STAGE 5 - collect, keep every shift once (the report takes the distinct Shift values: Afternoon, Blue, Day, Gold, Green, Night, Red), decide, parquet, path, write object.

5.2 Keep distinct shifts
5.3 Decide pbi_shift_naming
5.4 Set pbi_shift_naming path
[6] pbi_calendar
info: STAGE 6 - generated, no file: one row per date from CALENDAR_START to CALENDAR_END in 1.1 (2011-01-01 to 2050-12-31 as in the report, 14610 rows), Monday week start, ISO week number. Dates are text YYYY-MM-DD.

name: 6.1 Build calendar rows
6.2 Set pbi_calendar path
[7] ERRORS
info: STAGE 7 - a catch node takes every error raised by a node of this tab and turns it into a log line with the name of the node and the message of the API (for example the limit message of evaluateKPIs). Errors of the log nodes themselves are not logged again.

name: 7.1 Describe error
[8] LOG
info: STAGE 8 - every log line arrives here through the link "to LOG". 1 turns a line into a row (time, flow, site, production day, level) and shows it in the debug sidebar. The join collects the rows for 30 s, the delay lets one batch pass every 10 s so two writes do not overlap, 3 sets the file of the month and the read node loads the old file. A read of a file that does not exist answers nothing (only a warning), so the same batch also goes through a 10 s wait to the append step. The log is written whatever the dry-run switch says.

name: 8.1 Format log line
8.2 Build log write
[9] LOG WRITE
info: STAGE 9 - adds the rows of the batch to the old file and writes the whole file back (the data lake has no append). Columns: ts_utc, seq, flow, site, production_day, mode, level, source, message. Every field is quoted, line breaks become a space. The batch arrives twice (read answer and the wait) and is written once. If the read gives no answer for a file this flow wrote before, a new file with a time stamp is written, so the history is never replaced.
